Hi Jake / team,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Attached is our proposed set of redlines (Orchid_MSARedlines_v3.docx) focused on the limitation of liability and exclusions for confidentiality/trade secrets. High-level summary:

- We can accept a narrowly tailored carve-out to the liability cap for damages resulting from unauthorized disclosure or misappropriation of Trade Secrets and Confidential Information, but it needs to be limited.
- Our proposed language: carve-out applies only to damages attributable to willful and malicious misappropriation of trade secrets or intentional confidentiality breaches proven in a court of competent jurisdiction; incidental/accidental disclosures remain governed by the general cap.
- We do not accept open-ended consequential/indirect damages for any claim.

Please review the redline. If you prefer alternative phrasing (e.g., "gross negligence" vs. "willful and malicious"), flag it and we'll route to legal.

Attachments: Orchid_MSARedlines_v3.docx (tracked changes)

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether your security team requires audit rights tied to a carve-out.
2) If the scope above is acceptable, we can finalize OForm and move to DocuSign this week.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks

Jake / Dylan —

Thanks for the note. Quick legal framing and proposed replacement language below. Keeping it narrow will help us (and you) avoid open-ended exposure while still addressing true trade secret theft.

Proposed approach (three bullets):
1) Trigger: carve-out limited to damages resulting from proven, intentional misappropriation of Trade Secrets or intentional breach of confidentiality obligations ("Intentional Misappropriation"). We should avoid "negligence" as a trigger because that broadens exposure significantly.
2) Remedies: carve-out applies only to direct monetary damages awarded by a court or agreed in settlement; no recovery of punitive, exemplary, or consequential damages even if the claim arises from Intentional Misappropriation.
3) Caps within carve-out: in the event of Intentional Misappropriation, recoverable damages shall not exceed the greater of (a) actual direct damages or (b) two (2) times the fees paid under the Order Form in the preceding 12 months, subject to the carve-out trigger.

Suggested redline snippet (simple):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, liability cap set forth in Section X shall not apply to direct monetary damages finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction, or agreed in settlement, that result from Intentional Misappropriation of the other party's Trade Secrets or intentional breach of Confidential Information obligations; provided, however, that such recoverable damages shall not include consequential or punitive damages and shall be limited to the greater of actual direct damages or two (2) times the fees paid under the applicable Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."

Notes:
- We are open to replacing "Intentional Misappropriation" with "willful and malicious conduct" if you prefer that formulation.
- If Orchid insists on audit rights tied to the carve-out, we need a narrowly scoped, on-site/remote audit right limited to the incident and with a mutually agreed scope and confidentiality protections.

Attached: redline_summary.pdf (one-page rationale + tracked language)

Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

If the above is acceptable, I will prepare the DocuSign package once we have: (i) confirmation on audit/indemnity positions and (ii) PO attached.
